text: An ear lobe can be a normally developed free lobe or an attached hypoplastic lobe.
The upper edge of the ear can be positioned above the eyebrow, level with the eyebrow tail, level with the upper eyelid, or level with the exocanthion.
The helix of the ear can be described as flat, normally rolled, or wide.
A mouth dislocated from the central position of the face results in asymmetrical lengths of the labial fissure halves.
Depict the forehead as high by using a vertical surface, rather than tilting it dorsally.
A vertical or protruding forehead appears high, whereas a posterior tilt of the forehead reduces its projected height when viewed from the front.
A greatly protruding forehead makes the supraorbital rims appear depressed.
A concave upper face in a dish-like face may appear vertically shorter than it is in reality.
A receding mandible makes the lower face height appear small, while a protruding mandible contributes to the impression of a long face.
A deep nasal root makes the space between the orbits appear relatively narrow.
A flat nasofrontal angle combined with a deep nasal root and an acute nasolabial angle makes the nose appear long.
Depict the forehead with a backward tilt rather than a vertical or forward-tilted surface for adult and older subjects.
Uneven eyebrow levels or a hairline that is lower on one side indicate forehead asymmetry.
Differences in the height of the commissures of the labial fissure (mouth corners) indicate vertical asymmetry.
Uneven levels of the eyebrows, endocanthions, or eye fissures indicate vertical asymmetry.
Flatter facial contours give the impression of a smaller facial half.
condition: when observing facial depth and contours

text: A small height of the palpebral fissure relative to its width indicates ptosis.
An anteverted nasal tip is characterized by an upper lip inclination that is vertical or protruding rather than negative.
Depict a wide mouth by making the horizontal width of the mouth large relative to the width of the face.
Depict a narrow mouth by making the horizontal width of the mouth small relative to the width of the face.
Depict a protrusive upper lip by increasing the inclination of the upper lip forward.
Depict wide/short ears by increasing the ratio of ear width to ear length.
Depict narrow/long ears by decreasing the ratio of ear width to ear length.
Depict high-set ears by placing the ears higher on the head relative to craniofacial height.
Depict low-set ears by placing the ears lower on the head relative to craniofacial height.
Depict ears with high inclination by tilting the medial longitudinal axis of the ear backward.
Attractive women have eyes with higher fissure height and a higher tilt.
A higher degree of nasal bridge deviation is a sign of a below-average attractiveness in both men and women.
Ensure hair does not cover the ears to allow for the display of asymmetry in ear location.
Depict a Chinese (CP) head as brachycephalic, meaning relatively short and wide.
Depict an African American (AA) head as dolichocephalic, meaning relatively elongated and narrow.
Chinese faces are characterized by a wider facial width (zy-zy) compared to African-American or Caucasian faces.
African-American faces have a higher facial index (n-gn/zy-zy) than Chinese faces.
Chinese faces have a lower facial index (n-gn/zy-zy) than Caucasian or African-American faces.
In Chinese (CP) individuals, the upper lip height is relatively high in relation to the mouth width.
Depict ears as relatively wide and short for an African-American character.
Depict ears as relatively narrow and long for a Chinese character.
